NodeService（C++）

Service introduction

NodeService is Atom SDK A dedicated service for node operations in the main graph, providing capabilities such as node addition and deletion, port connection, parameter reading and writing, and port data reading. All operations operate on the main graph (the top-level graph), as opposed to the subgraphs inside the subgraph nodes of the GraphNodeService operation.

Header file:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
// or quoted individually(Pass client.hpp automatically included)
#include "atom_sdk/services/node.hpp"

Entrance:

atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
atom::sdk::NodeService& ns = client.node();

Applicable scenarios

  • Dynamically add and delete nodes in the opened main graph

  • Edit port connections between nodes and build data flows

  • Write JSON parameters for the node or upload the model file as a parameter

  • Read node port output data (image, point cloud, JSON)

Recommended calling order

client.graph().open_graph(graph_name)
           ↓
     create_node           ← Add nodes to the graph
           ↓
  set_node_param_data      ← Write node parameters(many times)
           ↓_nodes         ← Connect node port(many times)
           ↓
     initia↓
          ↓
     activate_node         ← Activate node
           ↓
   client.graph().run_graph(graph_name)
           |
           ↓port_data      ← Read output

Interface detailed explanation

create_node

JsonObject create_node(const CreateNodeParams& params) const;

Purpose: Create a new node of the specified type in the main graph.

parameters type Description

params.graph_name

std::string

Target map name (must be open)

params.node_name

std::string

node type name (needs to be in the type list returned by get_all_nodes_info)

*Return value: * JsonObject, containing new node information:

field type Description

nodeId

string

The unique ID of the new node, you need to use this ID for subsequent operations

name

string

Node type name

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");

    // Open the picture first
    client.graph().open_graph("my_graph");

    // Create node
    auto result = client.node().create_node(
        {"my_graph", "YoloDetectionNode"});

    std::string node_id = result.at("nodeId").get<std::string>();
    std::cout << "Create node ID:" << node_id << std::endl;
    std::cout << "Request status:" << result.at("status").get<std::int64_t>() << std::endl;

    return 0;
}

create_dynamic_io_node

JsonObject create_dynamic_io_node(const CreateDynamicNodeParams& params) const;

Purpose: Create nodes with dynamic input and output definitions in the main graph.

auto dynamic_node = client.node().create_dynamic_io_node({
    "demo_graph",
    "DynamicNode",
    atom::sdk::json::parse(R"({"inputs":[{"name":"image_in"}]})")
});

change_node_io

JsonObject change_node_io(const ChangeNodeIOParams& params) const;

Purpose: Modify the input and output structure of dynamic nodes.

client.node().change_node_io({
    "demo_graph",
    atom::sdk::json::value_to<std::string>(dynamic_node.at("nodeId")),
    atom::sdk::json::parse(R"({"outputs":[{"name":"mask_out"}]})")
});

create_node_by_copy

JsonObject create_node_by_copy(const CopyNodeParams& params) const;

Purpose: Use the existing node in the graph as a template to copy a new node of the same type, retaining the parameter configuration of the copied node.

parameters type Description

params.graph_name

std::string

Picture name

params.node_name

std::string

Node type name

params.node_id

std::string

ID of the copied node

*Return value: * JsonObject, contains new node information, the structure is the same as create_node.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    client.graph().open_graph("my_graph");

    // Get the source node first ID(Assume known)
    std::string source_node_id = "node_abc123";

    auto result = client.node().create_node_by_copy(
        {"my_graph", "YoloDetectionNode", source_node_id});

    std::string new_id = result.at("nodeId").get<std::string>();
    std::cout << "Copy to get new node ID:" << new_id << std::endl;
    std::cout << "Request status:" << result.at("status").get<std::int64_t>() << std::endl;

    return 0;
}

create_graph_node

JsonObject create_graph_node(const CreateGraphNodeParams& params) const;

Use: Create a graph node based on an existing subgraph.

auto graph_node = client.node().create_graph_node(
    {"demo_graph", "SubFlow", "sub_graph_alpha"});

The node to be deleted ID

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"

int main() {

connect_nodes

JsonObject connect_nodes(const NodeConnectionParams& params) const;

Purpose: Connect the output port of one node to the input port of another node to establish a data flow edge.

parameters type Description

params.graph_name

std::string

Picture name

params.output_node_id

std::string

The node that outputs data (upstream node) ID

params.output_port_name

std::string

The output port name of the upstream node

params.input_node_id

std::string

Node receiving data (downstream node)ID

params.input_port_name

std::string

Input port name of downstream node

*Return value: * JsonObject, including connection result information.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    client.graph().open_graph("my_graph");

    // Will preprocess node's "image_out" The port connected to the detection node "image_in" port
    auto result = client.node().connect_nodes(
        {"my_graph", "preprocess_node_id", "image_out", "detect_node_id", "image_in"});

    std::cout << "Connection successful" << std::endl;

    return 0;
}

get_node_params

JsonObject get_node_params(const NodeRef& params) const;

Purpose: Read the current parameter snapshot of the node to check whether the parameter configuration is correct.

parameters type Description

params.graph_name

std::string

Picture name

params.node_id

std::string

Node ID

*Return value: * JsonObject, contains the current values of all parameters of the node. The specific fields vary depending on the node type.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    client.graph().open_graph("my_graph");

    auto params = client.node().get_node_params({"my_graph", "node_abc123"});

    // Traverse and print all parameters
    for (const auto& [key, val] : params) {
        std::cout << "parameters " << key << std::endl;
    }

    return 0;
}

get_node_info_in_graph

JsonObject get_node_info_in_graph(const NodeRef& params) const;

Purpose: Read the complete information of the node in the main graph, including port list, connection relationship and parameter definition.

parameters type Description

params.graph_name

std::string

Picture name

params.node_id

std::string

Node ID

*Return value: * JsonObject, containing complete node information.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    client.graph().open_graph("my_graph");

    auto info = client.node().get_node_info_in_graph({"my_graph", "node_abc123"});

    if (info.contains("name")) {
        std::string name = info.at("name").get<std::string>();
        std::cout << "Node name:" << name << std::endl;
    }

    return 0;
}

get_node_port_data

PortDataResult get_node_port_data(const PortRef& params) const;

Purpose: Read the output data of the specified port of the node (JSON format), while carrying attachments (such as image bytes).

parameters type Description

params.graph_name

std::string

Picture name

params.node_id

std::string

Node ID

params.port_name

std::string

Port name

params.io_type

std::string

port type, usually "outputs" or "inputs"

Return value: PortDataResult Structure:

field type Description

data

JsonObject JSON data output from

port

attachments

std::unordered_map<std::string, ByteBuffer>

attachment map, key is the attachment name, value is the original byte

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");

    // Read port data after the graph is completed
    auto run_result = client.graph().run_graph("detection_graph");
    std::cout << "Request status:" << run_result.at("status").get<std::int64_t>() << std::endl;

    atom::sdk::PortDataResult port_data = client.node().get_node_port_data(
        {"detection_graph", "detect_node_id", "detection_result", "outputs"});

    // read JSON data
    const auto& data = port_data.data;
    if (data.contains("detections")) {
        const auto& dets = data.at("detections");
        std::cout << "Number of test results:" << dets.size() << std::endl;

        for (const auto& det : dets) {
            const auto& obj = det;
            double confidence = obj.at("confidence").get<double>();
            std::cout << "  Confidence:" << confidence << std::endl;
        }
    }

    // Read attachment(such as visual images)
    if (port_data.attachments.count("vis_image") > 0) {
        const auto& img_bytes = port_data.attachments.at("vis_image");
        std::cout << "Visualization image size:" << img_bytes.size() << " bytes" << std::endl;
    }

    return 0;
}

download_data

JsonObject download_data(const PortRef& params) const;

Purpose: Generate download links for node port data. It is suitable for scenarios where the port output is large and you want to hand it over to the front end or other tools to download according to the link.

parameters type Description

params.graph_name

std::string

Picture name

params.node_id

std::string

Node ID

params.port_name

std::string

Port name

params.io_type

std::string

port type, usually "outputs" or "inputs"

*Return value: * JsonObject, including the download information returned by the server.

Example:

auto download = client.node().download_data(
    {"detection_graph", "detect_node_id", "detection_result", "outputs"});

get_points_data_parsed

std::vector<ParsedPointCloud> get_points_data_parsed(
    const PortRef& params) const;

Purpose: Directly read and parse node point clouds, it is recommended to use it first.

Example:

auto clouds = client.node().get_points_data_parsed(
    {"lidar_graph", "point_cloud_node_id", "pc_out", "outputs"});

get_points_data

ByteBuffer get_points_data(const PortRef& params) const;

Purpose: Read the raw byte stream of the node point cloud class port.

parameters type Description

params.graph_name

std::string

Picture name

params.node_id

std::string

Node ID

params.port_name

std::string

Point cloud output port name

params.io_type

std::string

port type, usually "outputs"

*Return value: * ByteBuffer (std::vector<uint8_t>), server raw binary data. Note: * What is returned here is not a "pure point coordinate array" * The bytes of Node/GetPointsData are preceded by Atom’s own point cloud header information. * In ordinary scenarios, it is recommended to use the above get_points_data_parsed() first.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <cstring>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    auto run_result = client.graph().run_graph("lidar_graph");
    std::cout << "Request status:" << run_result.at("status").get<std::int64_t>() << std::endl;

    atom::sdk::ByteBuffer raw = client.node().get_points_data(
        {"lidar_graph", "point_cloud_node_id", "pc_out", "outputs"});

    std::cout << "raw bytes: " << raw.size() << std::endl;

    return 0;
}

set_node_param_data

JsonObject set_node_param_data(const NodeParamUpdate& params) const;

Purpose: Writes a JSON value to the node’s specified parameter.

parameters type Description

params.graph_name

std::string

Picture name

params.node_id

std::string

Node ID

params.param_name

std::string

Parameter name

params.param_type

std::string

parameter category, usually "init_params" or "run_params"

params.value

JsonValue / std::filesystem::path

JSON value or file path to write

*Return value: * JsonObject, operation result.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include "atom_sdk/core/json.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    client.graph().open_graph("my_graph");

    std::string node_id = "detect_node_id";

    // Write numeric parameters(confidence threshold)
    atom::sdk::JsonValue threshold = 0.6;
    client.node().set_node_param_data(
        {"my_graph", node_id, "confidence_threshold", "init_params", threshold});

    // Write string parameters
    atom::sdk::JsonValue model_type = "yolov8n";
    client.node().set_node_param_data(
        {"my_graph", node_id, "model_type", "init_params", model_type});

    // write JSON Object parameters
    atom::sdk::JsonObject config;
    config["nms_threshold"] = 0.4;
    config["max_detections"] = 100;
    atom::sdk::JsonValue config_val(config);
    client.node().set_node_param_data(
        {"my_graph", node_id, "nms_config", "init_params", config_val});

    std::cout << "Parameter setting completed" << std::endl;

    return 0;
}

set_node_param_data (file path value)

JsonObject set_node_param_data(const NodeParamUpdate& params) const;

Purpose: Automatically upload and write the contents of local files (such as model weights .onnx, configuration files, etc.) to node parameters. SDK handles file reading and uploading internally automatically.

parameters type Description

params.graph_name

std::string

Picture name

params.node_id

std::string

Node ID

params.param_name

std::string

Parameter name

params.param_type

std::string

parameter category, usually "init_params"

params.value

std::filesystem::path

local file path, SDK automatically reads and uploads file content

*Return value: * JsonObject, operation result.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <filesystem>
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    client.graph().open_graph("my_graph");

    std::string node_id = "detect_node_id";
    std::filesystem::path model_path = "/models/yolov8n.onnx";

    // upload ONNX Model files as node parameters
    auto result = client.node().set_node_param_data(
        {"my_graph", node_id, "model_file", "init_params", model_path});

    std::cout << "Model file upload completed" << std::endl;

    return 0;
}

set_binding_name

JsonObject set_binding_name(const NodeBindingUpdate& params) const;

Purpose: Set the externally exposed binding name for the node’s parameters or port, so that it can be accessed through the binding interface of RuntimeService.

parameters type Description

params.graph_name

std::string

Picture name

params.node_id

std::string

Node ID

params.binding_type

std::string

binding type, such as "outputs" or "init_params" etc.

params.origin_name

std::string

The original name of the port or parameter

params.binding_name

std::string

Exposed binding alias

*Return value: * JsonObject, operation result.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    client.graph().open_graph("my_graph");

    // will detect the node's "detection_result" Output bindings are externally visible "result"
    auto result = client.node().set_binding_name(
        {"my_graph", "detect_node_id", "outputs", "detection_result", "result"});

    std::cout << "Binding name set successfully" << std::endl;

    return 0;
}

activate_node

JsonObject activate_node(
    const NodeRef& params,
    std::optional<double> timeout_seconds = 30.0) const;

Purpose: Activate the node, usually called after initialization is completed, bringing the node into the ready state and triggering output checks. SDK will poll the server for responses until finish is true or exceeds timeout_seconds.

parameters type Description

params.graph_name

std::string

Picture name

params.node_id

std::string

Node ID

timeout_seconds

std::optional<double>

Polling waiting timeout, default is 30.0 seconds; passing std::nullopt means waiting until completion or the server reports an error

*Return value: * JsonObject, containing activation result information.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    client.graph().open_graph("my_graph");

    // Activate node after initialization
    client.node().initial_node({"my_graph", "detect_node_id"});
    client.node().activate_node({"my_graph", "detect_node_id"}, 60.0);

    return 0;
}

initial_node

JsonObject initial_node(const NodeRef& params) const;

Purpose: Initialize nodes, trigger node loading model, allocate resources and other initialization logic. Need to be called after setting all parameters.

parameters type Description

params.graph_name

std::string

Picture name

params.node_id

std::string

Node ID

*Return value: * JsonObject, containing initialization result information.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <filesystem>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    client.graph().open_graph("my_graph");

    std::string node_id = "detect_node_id";

    // Set parameters first
    client.node().set_node_param_data(
        {"my_graph", node_id, "model_file", "init_params",
         std::filesystem::path("/models/yolov8n.onnx")});

    // Reinitialize(Trigger model loading)
    auto result = client.node().initial_node({"my_graph", node_id});

    return 0;
}

update_node

JsonObject update_node(const NodeRef& params) const;

Purpose: Update node configuration and trigger recalculation, usually called after dynamically modifying parameters at runtime. This interface only initiates one request as defined by the server UpdateNode and does not poll finish; if the server returns finish=false, SDK will also return this response directly to the caller.

parameters type Description

params.graph_name

std::string

Picture name

params.node_id

std::string

Node ID

*Return value: * JsonObject, update result.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    client.graph().open_graph("my_graph");

    // Trigger update after modifying parameters
    atom::sdk::JsonValue new_threshold = 0.7;
    client.node().set_node_param_data(
        {"my_graph", "detect_node_id", "confidence_threshold", "run_params", new_threshold});
    client.node().update_node({"my_graph", "detect_node_id"});

    return 0;
}

Complete example

The following shows the complete main graph node editing and running process:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <filesystem>
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    try {
        atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
        auto& gs = client.graph();
        auto& ns = client.node();

        // 1. Create and open diagram
        gs.create_graph({"pipeline_graph", "Testing pipeline"});
        gs.open_graph("pipeline_graph");

        // 2. Create a preprocessing node
        auto preproc = ns.create_node({"pipeline_graph", "ImagePreprocessNode", "Image preprocessing"});
        std::string preproc_id = preproc.at("nodeId").get<std::string>();

        // 3. Create detection node
        auto detect = ns.create_node({"pipeline_graph", "YoloDetectionNode", "Target detection"});
        std::string detect_id = detect.at("nodeId").get<std::string>();

        // 4. Set detection node parameters:Upload model file
        ns.set_node_param_data(
            {"pipeline_graph", detect_id, "model_file", "init_params",
             std::filesystem::path("/models/yolov8n.onnx")});

        // 5. Set operating parameters(JSON value)
        atom::sdk::JsonValue threshold = 0.5;
        ns.set_node_param_data(
            {"pipeline_graph", detect_id, "confidence_threshold", "run_params", threshold});

        // 6. Connect two nodes
        ns.connect_nodes(
            {"pipeline_graph", preproc_id, "image_out", detect_id, "image_in"});

        // 7. Initialize and activate nodes
        ns.initial_node({"pipeline_graph", detect_id});
        ns.activate_node({"pipeline_graph", detect_id});

        // 8. Run the entire graph
        auto run_result = gs.run_graph("pipeline_graph");
        std::cout << "[8] Request status:" << run_result.at("status").get<std::int64_t>() << std::endl;

        // 9. Read detection node output
        auto port_data = ns.get_node_port_data(
            {"pipeline_graph", detect_id, "detection_result", "outputs"});

        const auto& data = port_data.data;
        std::cout << "Number of port data fields:" << data.size() << std::endl;

        // 10. Read attachment(Visualization images)
        if (port_data.attachments.count("vis_image") > 0) {
            const auto& img = port_data.attachments.at("vis_image");
            std::cout << "Visualization image bytes:" << img.size() << std::endl;
        }

        // 11. clean up
        gs.clear_graph("pipeline_graph");
        gs.release_graph("pipeline_graph");

    } catch (const atom::sdk::AtomError& e) {
        std::cerr << "SDK Error:" << e.what() << std::endl;
        return 1;
    }

    return 0;
}
